slot.brief: Energy-level diagram of hydrogen with a few marked transitions; identify which jump emits a given spectral series photon and compute its wavelength.

stem: Four transitions $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ in a hydrogen atom are shown in the figure. The transition that corresponds to the emission of the first line of the Balmer series and its emitted wavelength are (take Rydberg constant $R = 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}$):

verdicts.working: First Balmer line is n=3 → n=2, which is transition B in the figure. 1/λ = R(1/2² − 1/3²) = 5R/36, so λ = 36/(5×1.097×10⁷) ≈ 656 nm. (486 nm corresponds to A: 4→2; 122 nm to D: 2→1.)

working:
1. Spectral series identification: The Balmer series corresponds to electron transitions terminating at the lower energy level $n_1 = 2$.
2. Line identification: The first line of the Balmer series ($H_\alpha$) represents the transition from the adjacent higher state $n_2 = 3$ to $n_1 = 2$. In the diagram, this downward jump from $n = 3$ to $n = 2$ is labelled as transition $B$.
3. Wavelength calculation using the Rydberg formula:
$$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right) = R \left(\dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2}\right) = R \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{5R}{36}$$
$$\lambda = \dfrac{36}{5R} = \dfrac{36}{5 \times 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}} = \dfrac{36}{5.485 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}} \approx 6.563 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \approx 656\text{ nm}$$

Independent check: First Balmer line is n=3 → n=2, which is transition B in the figure. 1/λ = R(1/2² − 1/3²) = 5R/36, so λ = 36/(5×1.097×10⁷) ≈ 656 nm. (486 nm corresponds to A: 4→2; 122 nm to D: 2→1.)

figure.description: An energy-level diagram showing four horizontal parallel lines representing principal quantum numbers $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$ of a hydrogen atom. The vertical spacing between lines decreases going upward. Each horizontal line is labelled on the right with its quantum number ($n = 1$ at the bottom, followed by $n = 2$, $n = 3$, and $n = 4$ at the top) and on the left with its energy value ($-13.6\text{ eV}$ for $n = 1$, $-3.4\text{ eV}$ for $n = 2$, $-1.51\text{ eV}$ for $n = 3$, and $-0.85\text{ eV}$ for $n = 4$). Four downward-pointing vertical arrows are drawn between the levels: arrow A extends from $n = 4$ down to $n = 2$; arrow B extends from $n = 3$ down to $n = 2$ (to the right of A); arrow C extends from $n = 3$ down to $n = 1$ (to the right of B); arrow D extends from $n = 2$ down to $n = 1$ (to the right of C). Each arrow has its corresponding capital letter label (A, B, C, D) positioned beside the middle of its shaft.
